# Card art: the cards still missing a picture (generated by `pnpm cardprompts:missing`: do not edit by hand)

86 cards: 86 with no picture, 0 showing a borrowed copy of another card's picture. Nine to a sheet, best cards first in each character.

## How to use
1. Start with [missing-batch-01.md](missing-batch-01.md) (the first sheet of every character: their best cards). Paste ONE prompt at a time into the image AI and attach the Valeria image (`Sunlit Paladin with Shield and Sword.png`) as the style anchor.
2. Check that the pictures are separate, in a clean 3 x 3 grid, with no text. If a picture is wrong, regenerate the whole sheet (I cut by position).
3. Each prompt ends by asking ChatGPT to save the picture as a PNG with the right name (for example `knight-m01.png`) and give a download link: download it into `assets-src/cards/`. If it hands back a plain image instead, save it under the name in the sheet heading.
4. Tell me which sheets are in: I cut them (`tools/pack-cards.ps1`) and run this tool again, so only what is still missing is listed. That run moves the sheets that were cut into `assets-src/cards/_cut/` (their card lists are kept in `sheets-cut.json`, and `pack-cards.ps1` still reads them there), because the next sheets reuse the names from -m01.

| Character | Cards | Sheets |
|---|---|---|
| Shaman | 83 | 10 |
| Drunkard | 3 | 1 |

## Shaman

### Sheet `shaman-m01` (9 pictures, rare first)

```
Create ONE ILLUSTRATION SHEET of 9 separate card-art pictures for a card-battler game (like Slay the Spire), 2400 x 1800, no text.
The attached image (Valeria) is the STYLE ANCHOR: match its cartoon game-art rendering exactly (bold clean dark outlines, flat saturated colours, simple cel shading, crisp polished shapes). Do NOT copy her character; paint scenes and objects. Backgrounds are softer and less contrasty than the main subject so the subject pops.

LAYOUT (critical): a clean 3 x 3 grid of landscape 4:3 pictures (each about 760 x 570), separated by thin flat dark navy (#14181f) gutters, with NO frames, NO borders, NO captions, NO text, NO numbers. Every picture fills its own cell completely; nothing crosses a gutter. Each picture has ONE clear subject in the middle that reads at thumbnail size, a simple scene behind it, light from the upper left.

WORLD: Ilvane, a spirit shaman who calls glowing totems. An elder shaman who casts Flame, Frost and Storm and keeps a row of totems. Each totem works every turn while it stands; when he commands it, its spirit acts once more and is gone, and a new one takes its place at the back of the row. World: a teal-and-orange foundry of machines: hazard stripes, steel, glowing cyan, sparks and steam.

THE PICTURES, in this exact order, left to right, top row first. Use the card name and its effect only to decide what to draw; never write the name:
1. "Absolute Zero" (attack): Frost. Deal 10 (+3 per Faltering on each) damage to ALL enemies. Apply 2 Faltering to ALL enemies. Show a dynamic strike caught mid-action. A little more dramatic and detailed.
2. "Avalanche" (attack): Frost. Deal 14 damage to ALL enemies. Apply 1 Faltering to ALL enemies. Show a dynamic strike caught mid-action. A little more dramatic and detailed.
3. "Call the Elder Tree" (skill): Plant an Elder Tree. Show a defensive or tactical moment, calm and clear. A little more dramatic and detailed.
4. "Call the Moon Owl" (skill): Plant a Moon Owl. Show a defensive or tactical moment, calm and clear. A little more dramatic and detailed.
5. "Calm Before the Storm" (aura): At the start of your turn: Apply 3 Sapped to ALL enemies until the end of their next turn. Show a grand symbolic still-life: one iconic object or pose that stands for the idea. A little more dramatic and detailed.
6. "Carve the Spirit Pole" (skill): Gain a totem position. Plant a random totem. Draw 1 card. Show a defensive or tactical moment, calm and clear. A little more dramatic and detailed.
7. "Eye of the Tempest" (attack): Storm. Deal 11 damage to 4 different random enemies (25% more when only one enemy stands). Show a dynamic strike caught mid-action. A little more dramatic and detailed.
8. "Flashpoint" (attack): Flame. Deal 4 (+3 per Burn on the target) damage. Consume. Show a dynamic strike caught mid-action. A little more dramatic and detailed.
9. "Frostbound" (aura): Whenever you put a debuff on an enemy: Gain 3 Barrier. Show a grand symbolic still-life: one iconic object or pose that stands for the idea. A little more dramatic and detailed.

NEGATIVE: text, letters, numbers, captions, labels, UI, card frames, borders, watermark, logo, photorealism, gritty texture, nudity, characters facing away.

FILE: when the image is done, save it as a PNG file named exactly shaman-m01.png and give me a download link to that file.
```

Create ONE ILLUSTRATION SHEET of 2 separate card-art pictures for a card-battler game (like Slay the Spire), 2400 x 1800, no text.

WORLD: Ilvane, a spirit shaman who calls glowing totems. An elder shaman who casts Flame, Frost and Storm and keeps a row of totems. Each totem works every turn while it stands; when he commands it, its spirit acts once more and is gone, and a new one takes its place at the back of the row. World: a teal-and-orange foundry of machines: hazard stripes, steel, glowing cyan, sparks and steam.

THE PICTURES, in this exact order, left to right, top row first. Use the card name and its effect only to decide what to draw; never write the name:
